# New renderings — iliad-040 (Iliad 6.440–529)

Rows in the format of the table in `conventions.md`: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἑλκεσίπεπλος (Τρῳάδας ἑλκεσιπέπλους, 6.442) | "trailing-robed" | "with their trailing robes" | "long-robed" (kept for τανύπεπλος, the Odyssey's "long-robed"), "with flowing robes", "trailing their gowns"; ἕλκω "drag" + πέπλος "robe" |
| αἰδέομαι + accusative of persons (6.442) | "I feel shame before" | "I am ashamed before" | "I respect", "I revere" (the table's sense for αἰδέομαι at 4.402, 14.388); here the word is shame before others' opinion, and the note says so |
| ἀλυσκάζω (νόσφιν ἀλυσκάζω πολέμοιο, 6.443) | "I shun" | "hold aloof from … shunning it" | "skulk", "evade"; "dodging" (the Iliad table's 5.253 row, "by dodging") is not carried over: the Odyssey's "shunning" (17.581) is the binding base, and the 5.253 row, shipped without a note on the choice, is left as it stands; the verb is ἀλύσκω "avoid" lengthened |
| κακὸς ὣς (of a man in battle, 6.443) | "like a base man" | "like a base man" | "like a coward"; keeps the table's κακός "base" (2.365, 4.299), the note says cowardly |
| ἐλεύθερον ἦμαρ (6.455) · ἐλεύθερον κρητῆρα (6.528) | "the day of freedom" · "a mixing-bowl of freedom" | "your day of freedom" · "a mixing-bowl of freedom" | "the free day", "a free bowl", "a bowl for the free"; matches the table’s δούλιον ἦμαρ "day of slavery" |
| ἱστόν ὑφαίνοις (6.456) | "weave the web" | "weave a web" | "work the loom" (kept for ἱστόν at 6.491 and the shipped Odyssey 1.357, where the loom is the thing she tends; iliad-001 has "plies the loom" for ἱστὸν ἐποιχομένην); ἱστόν ὑφαίνω is "weave a web" as at 3.125 and iliad-017 (3.125 is the table row, "web"), and the note at 6.456 says it is the web being woven |
| χυτὴ γαῖα (6.464) | "the heaped earth" | "the heaped earth" | "poured-out earth", "the mound"; follows the Odyssey's "heaped up a mound of earth" / "heaped earth over him" (3.258, odyssey-011) and the Iliad's "heaped a tomb" (6.419) |
| ἑλκηθμός (σοῦ ἑλκηθμοῖο, 6.465; rare noun from ἕλκω) | "your being dragged away" | "your being dragged away" | "your dragging", "your abduction", "your captivity" |
| ἱππιοχαίτης (λόφον ἱππιοχαίτην, 6.469) | "horse-maned" | "horse-maned" | "horsehair" (reserved for ἱπποδάσεια), "horse-tailed" (ἵππουρις), "crested" (λόφος); ἵππος + χαίτη "mane" |
| ἀτύζομαι, aorist participle ἀτυχθείς (6.468, of the child) | "dazed with fear" | "dazed with fear" | "frightened", "terrified" (kept for ταρβέω); follows the table's ἀτυζόμενος (6.38) |
| ταρβήσας χαλκόν (6.469) | "terrified at the bronze" | "terrified by the bronze" | "fearing", "afraid of" |
| κηώδης (κηώδεϊ κόλπῳ, 6.483) | "fragrant" | "fragrant" | "sweet-smelling", "perfumed", "incense-scented" |
| δακρυόεν γελάσασα (6.484) | "laughing tearfully" | "laughing through her tears" | "smiling", "weeping and laughing" |
| χειρί τέ μιν κατέρεξεν ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζε (6.485, male subject, female object) | "and stroked her with his hand, and spoke a word, and called her by name:" | "and stroked her with his hand, and spoke, calling her by name:" | the table's 4.610 row with "her" for μιν, as the 1.361 row has it with "her hand" |
| προϊάψει (6.487; the verb of 1.3 προΐαψεν) | "will send forth" | "will fling me down to Hades" | "will send me to Hades", "will hurl"; keeps 1.3's "flung … down to Hades" |
| μοῖραν … φημι πεφυγμένον ἔμμεναι (6.488) | "fate … has escaped" | "has escaped his fate" | "destiny", "doom" (reserved for πότμος, κήρ); μοῖρα "fate" |
| ἄλοχος … ἐντροπαλιζομένη (6.496) | "turning back again and again" | "turning back again and again" | "looking back over and over", "turning round and round"; ἐν + τρέπω, frequentative; the note says she is looking back |
| ἀμφίπολος (6.491, 6.499) | "handmaid" | "handmaid" | "attendants" (the Odyssey table's plural ἀμφίπολοι, 6.18 and elsewhere; the Iliad has "handmaids" at 3.143, 3.422, iliad-017 and -020, and iliad-039 at 6.372 and 6.399, and the 6.389 row keeps "handmaid" for this noun); the Iliad's house word for ἀμφίπολος is "handmaid(s)", fixed at review. iliad-038 ships "attendants" at 6.286 and 6.323 and is not touched here (see review.md) |
| κραιπνοῖσι ποσὶ πεποιθώς (6.505) | "trusting in his rushing feet" | "trusting in his rushing feet" | "swift feet" (kept for ταχέες πόδες, 5.885), "nimble"; follows the table's κραιπνός "rushing" |
| σεύατο (6.505) | "rushed" | "rushed" | "darted", "hurried"; σεύω "rush" (2.12) |
| στατὸς ἵππος (6.506) | "stalled horse" | "stalled horse" | "tethered horse", "standing horse" |
| ἀκοστήσας ἐπὶ φάτνῃ (6.506; rare verb from ἀκοστή "barley") | "fed on barley at the manger" | "fed on barley at the manger" | "grown wanton", "well fed", "full of oats" |
| κροαίνων (6.507; rare verb) | "pounding" | "pounding" | "galloping", "stamping", "thundering" |
| ἐϋρρεῖος ποταμοῖο (6.508) | "of the fair-flowing river" | "the fair-flowing river" | "of the broad-flowing river", "of the lovely stream"; ἐϋρρεής "fair-flowing", as the table's ἐϋρρείτης |
| χαῖται … ἀΐσσονται (6.509–510) | "the mane streams" | "his mane streams" | "the manes dart", "the manes fly" |
| ἀγλαΐηφι πεποιθώς (6.510, of a horse) | "trusting in his splendour" | "trusting in his beauty" | follows the table's ἀγλαΐη (18.180) "splendour" / "beauty" |
| ῥίμφα (6.511) | "lightly" | "lightly" | "swiftly" (reserved for θοός, ὠκύς, ταχύς), "nimbly" |
| ἤθεα καὶ νομὸν ἵππων (6.511) | "the haunts and pasture of the horses" | "the haunts and pasture of the horses" | "stables", "the meadow", "grazing grounds"; ἦθος "haunt" as the table's ἤθεα (14.411) |
| ἠλέκτωρ (ὥς τ’ ἠλέκτωρ, 6.513; rare word) | "like the sun" | "like the sun" (+ note: usual explanation, sense not certain; confirmed at review: the word occurs nowhere else in the Iliad's published parts, the Odyssey's ἠλέκτρου / ἠλέκτροισιν are "amber", a different word) | "like amber" (ἤλεκτρον), "like a star", "like the beaming one" |
| καγχαλόων (6.514) | "exulting" | "exulting" | "laughing aloud", "boasting"; follows καγχαλόωσα "exulting" (23.1) |
| ἔτετμεν (6.515) | "found" | "came upon" | "met", "overtook"; aorist of a verb with no present in Homer |
| ὀαρίζω (ᾗ ὀάριζε γυναικί, 6.516) | "was conversing with" | "had been talking with" | "dallying with", "whispering with"; the note says it is intimate talk |
| ἐσσύμενον κατερύκω (6.518) | "even as you hasten … I am holding you back" | "hurrying as you are … am I holding you back" | "delaying", "detaining" |
| ἐναίσιμος (ὃς ἐναίσιμος εἴη, 6.521) · ἐναίσιμον (adverb, 6.519) | "one with a sense of what is fitting" · "in the fitting way" | "a sense of what is fitting" · "as was fitting" | "fair-minded", "just", "right-minded"; keeps the Odyssey's "fitting" |
| ἀτιμάζω (ἔργον ἀτιμήσειε μάχης, 6.522) | "would dishonour" | "would dishonour" | "belittle", "make light of", "despise"; keeps ἀτιμάζω "dishonour" (1.11) |
| μεθιεῖς (absolute, 6.523) | "you slacken" | "you slack off" | "you hold back", "you give up"; μεθίημι "slacken", no genitive here |
| κῆρ … θυμῷ together (τὸ δ’ ἐμὸν κῆρ ἄχνυται ἐν θυμῷ, 6.523–524) | "my heart grieves in my spirit" | "my heart grieves in my spirit" | "heart … heart"; κῆρ "heart", θυμός "spirit" where the two stand together, as the table's κραδίη θυμός τε (8.204) |
| αἴσχε’ ἀκούω (6.524) | "shameful things I hear" | "I hear shameful things said of you" | "insults", "reproaches", "slanders" |
| θεοῖς ἐπουρανίοισι αἰειγενέτῃσι (6.527, both epithets together) | "the gods of heaven, the forever-born" | "the everlasting gods of heaven" | "the immortal gods of heaven" (ἀθάνατος reserved); joins the table's ἐπουρανίοισι "of heaven" (6.129) and θεοῖς αἰειγενέτῃσι "the everlasting gods" (14.446) |
| κρητῆρα στήσασθαι ἐλεύθερον (6.528) | "to set up a mixing-bowl of freedom" | "set up a mixing-bowl of freedom" | "a free bowl"; στήσασθαι "set up for oneself"; κρητήρ "mixing-bowl" as in the table |

Note: ἠθεῖε reuses the table's ἠθεῖος row (14.147, sense not known; "honoured one" / "my honoured one", unchanged, with the note saying the sense is a guess), ἀρεσσόμεθ' the 4.362 row, and ὣς εἰπών / ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας the existing rows; none is a new choice.

Whole-line formula choices made here (these are the ones that will recur):

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὴν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε μέγας κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (6.440, whole-line speech introduction, feminine object) | "Her then in turn addressed great Hector of the glancing helmet:" | "Then great Hector of the glancing helmet spoke to her in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἀμείβομαι); follows the αὖτε προσέειπε rows (3.206, 16.58) with the table's μέγας κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (3.324) |
| τὸν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη κορυθαίολος Ἕκτωρ (6.520, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him answering addressed Hector of the glancing helmet:" | "In answer Hector of the glancing helmet said to him:" | "great" (the Greek has no μέγας here); follows the table's ἀπαμειβόμενος προσέφη rows |
| τὸν πρότερος προσέειπεν Ἀλέξανδρος θεοειδής (6.517, whole-line speech introduction) | "Him first addressed Alexander godlike-in-form:" | "Alexander, godlike in form, spoke to him first:" | follows the table's 5.276 row (πρότερος προσέειπε) |
| ἐκ δ’ ἐγέλασσε πατήρ τε φίλος καὶ πότνια μήτηρ (6.471) | "And aloud laughed his dear father and his lady mother;" | "His dear father and his lady mother laughed aloud;" | "queenly mother"; πότνια "lady" |
